discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated Hubbard-model physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Feynman proposed using one quantum system to emulate another. Jaksch, Zoller and coworkers (1998) showed that atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model. Greiner, Bloch and colleagues then observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (Nature 2002). This turned cold-atom physics into an experimental science of strongly correlated matter. Bloch and Greiner went on to develop quantum-gas microscopes with single-site resolution. With them they imaged Mott shells, antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string patterns, many-body localization and entanglement growth. Zoller's theoretical program set the blueprint for analog quantum simulators, including those built with trapped ions. Together this work has settled questions that numerics cannot easily reach and has made a new tool for condensed-matter physics and quantum information science. The platform now underpins many laboratories around the world.
